facebook_0900:
The trade that hurts most is often the one right after a good one.

That's why I stop after 1 or 2 good trades. The rule gets set before the session, not decided in the moment. After a good trade, the screen still looks full of opportunity. That's when traders start forcing setups that aren't there.

Every extra trade is one more chance to break a rule: a stop that's too wide, an early entry, a revenge trade after a loss.

So once I've had my good trade or two, the platform closes. The trades I already took stay the way I planned them.

Pick your stopping point before the open, write it down, and hold yourself to it.

I don't grade my trades while the chart is still moving.

My review happens at night, after work and after my son goes down for the night.

My New York session is long over by then, so there's no pull to jump back in and fix a red day. I look at two things: was the plan right, and did I follow it.

Calm eyes grade the process. Emotional eyes grade the P&L.
